environment.description: Node.js 18 Apollo Server v4 deployed on AWS ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The infrastructure uses AWS Secrets Manager automatic rotation with a Lambda rotator (rotation interval: 60 seconds) for the JWT_SIGNING_KEY. The ECS task definition references the secret ARN via `valueFrom` in the container secrets block, meaning the container receives the secret value at launch time. However, the task uses a sidecar container running a custom secrets-refresh daemon (image: internal/secrets-refresher:2.1.4) that polls Secrets Manager every 15 seconds and writes the current key to a shared tmpfs volume mounted at /run/secrets/jwt_current. The application reads JWT_SIGNING_KEY from this file on each request via a synchronous fs.readFileSync call patched into the validateToken function at deploy time through an init container that modifies the source. Additionally, the node-cache instance is configured with a post-rotation hook: the secrets-refresher sidecar sends SIGUSR2 to the Node.js process every rotation cycle, and the application has a process.on('SIGUSR2') handler that calls responseCache.flushAll(). The combination means: (1) any JWT signed with a previous key becomes invalid within 15 seconds maximum, and (2) any cached responses containing privileged data are purged every 60 seconds when rotation occurs, preventing cross-user cache poisoning from persisting beyond one rotation window.

config.secrets_rotation: AWS Secrets Manager Lambda rotator, 60s interval
config.cache_flush: SIGUSR2 handler calls responseCache.flushAll() on each rotation
config.effective_token_lifetime: max 60s before key rotates and old tokens rejected
